has_bug.instructions: Does `method` contain a concrete behavioral defect that a caller can reach?

criteria.true: For some input a caller can pass, the method returns a wrong result, leaves wrong state, throws when it should not, or fails to throw when it should
criteria.false: The method behaves correctly for every input its callers can pass; style, performance, and hypothetical misuse do not count

kind.instructions: If `method` has a defect, which kind is it?

criteria.boundary: An off-by-one, a wrong comparison, or a mishandled edge of a range
criteria.missing_null_handling: A null, undefined, empty, or absent value is not handled
criteria.wrong_return: The wrong value, or a value of the wrong shape, is returned for some input
criteria.swallowed_error: An error is caught, ignored, or turned into a misleading result
criteria.state_mutation: Shared or input state is mutated when it should not be, or left stale when it should change
criteria.ordering: Operations run in the wrong order, or rely on an order that is not guaranteed
criteria.resource_leak: A handle, lock, timer, process, or connection is not released on some path
criteria.inverted_condition: A condition, sign, or boolean is the wrong way round

severity.instructions: If something is wrong with `method`, how much would a caller feel it?
criteria: A wrong result in a rare case, or one the caller can see and recover from
A wrong result or wrong state in ordinary use
Data lost, corrupted, or exposed, or a check that should stop someone bypassed

refactor.instructions: Judging from `method`, its `metrics` (risk_score and maintainability_index run 0-100, cyclomatic_complexity and max_nesting are counts), and how its callers use it, what does it most need?

criteria.split: Does too many things; split it into smaller methods with one job each
criteria.flatten: Nested too deeply; flatten with early returns or extracted helpers
criteria.simplify_conditions: Conditions are hard to follow; simplify or name them
criteria.deduplicate: Repeats logic that exists elsewhere in the shown code; reuse it
criteria.rename: The name or parameters misdescribe what it does; rename them
criteria.remove_dead_code: Contains unreachable or unused code; remove it

does_what_it_claims.instructions: Does `method` do what its name, its parameters and its `leading_comment` say it does?

criteria.true: It behaves the way its name and its comment say it does
criteria.false: It does something different from, less than, or more than its name and comment say, so one of the two is wrong

documented.instructions: Could a caller learn what `method` promises from its `leading_comment`, or from the code itself where it is small enough to read?

criteria.true: Its contract, its edge cases and its side effects are all there to be read
criteria.false: A caller could not learn what it promises without reading it through. A comment that says something untrue is misaligned rather than this: this is what is missing.

exposed.instructions: Does a value chosen by someone outside this program reach `method`, or does `method` act outside the program on such a value?

criteria.true: Something a person or another system chose reaches it, such as a request, an argument, a message, a row, or a file whose name or contents they control; or it runs, queries, writes or sends using such a value.
criteria.false: Everything it works on was decided by this program, and anything it touches outside is named by this program.

injection.instructions: If `method` handles anything from outside the program: is this true of it? A value from outside is put into a shell command, a query, a path of execution, or anything that gets evaluated, without being escaped or parameterised.

criteria.true: Yes: a value from outside is put into a shell command, a query, a path of execution, or anything that gets evaluated, without being escaped or parameterised
criteria.false: No, or nothing from outside reaches this method

path_traversal.instructions: If `method` handles anything from outside the program: is this true of it? A name from outside is used to build a filesystem path, URL, or key without being confined to the place it is meant to reach.

criteria.true: Yes: a name from outside is used to build a filesystem path, URL, or key without being confined to the place it is meant to reach
criteria.false: No, or nothing from outside reaches this method

unsafe_deserialization.instructions: If `method` handles anything from outside the program: is this true of it? Data from outside is turned into code, or into an object whose type it chose. eval, new Function or a vm run over it; a deserializer that can instantiate arbitrary classes; a YAML or XML parser with tags or entities enabled; a merge that lets it set __proto__ or constructor. Parsing outside data into plain values is not this, however untrusted it is.

criteria.true: Yes: data from outside is turned into code, or into an object whose type it chose. eval, new Function or a vm run over it; a deserializer that can instantiate arbitrary classes; a YAML or XML parser with tags or entities enabled; a merge that lets it set __proto__ or constructor. Parsing outside data into plain values is not this, however untrusted it is.
criteria.false: No, or nothing from outside reaches this method

secret_exposure.instructions: If `method` handles anything from outside the program: is this true of it? A password, token, key, or other credential is written into the source, logged, returned to a caller, or sent somewhere it need not go.

criteria.true: Yes: a password, token, key, or other credential is written into the source, logged, returned to a caller, or sent somewhere it need not go
criteria.false: No, or nothing from outside reaches this method

missing_authorization.instructions: If `method` handles anything from outside the program: is this true of it? An action that should check who is asking, or what they may touch, does not check, or checks after it has already acted.

criteria.true: Yes: an action that should check who is asking, or what they may touch, does not check, or checks after it has already acted
criteria.false: No, or nothing from outside reaches this method

criteria.true: Security rests on predictable randomness, a home-made scheme, a broken algorithm, or a comparison that leaks timing
criteria.false: Nothing in `method` does this.

unvalidated_destination.instructions: If `method` handles anything from outside the program: is this true of it? An address, host, or redirect target from outside decides where a request or a user is sent.

criteria.true: Yes: an address, host, or redirect target from outside decides where a request or a user is sent
criteria.false: No, or nothing from outside reaches this method

resource_exhaustion.instructions: If `method` handles anything from outside the program: is this true of it? Input from outside decides how much memory, recursion, time or work happens, and nothing bounds it. Work whose size is what the operator asked for is not this: a tool doing as much work as the input it was pointed at is doing its job.

criteria.true: Yes: input from outside decides how much memory, recursion, time or work happens, and nothing bounds it. Work whose size is what the operator asked for is not this: a tool doing as much work as the input it was pointed at is doing its job.
criteria.false: No, or nothing from outside reaches this method

unsafe_reflection.instructions: If `method` handles anything from outside the program: is this true of it? A name from outside chooses which function, class, field or module is reached, so it picks code the program never named. An import or require built from it, a property taken off an object and called, a class or handler resolved by name. A lookup in a table the program itself wrote, where a name that is not in it is handled, is not this.

criteria.true: Yes: a name from outside chooses which function, class, field or module is reached, so it picks code the program never named. An import or require built from it, a property taken off an object and called, a class or handler resolved by name. A lookup in a table the program itself wrote, where a name that is not in it is handled, is not this.
criteria.false: No, or nothing from outside reaches this method

criteria.true: A check that exists is turned off or weakened: certificate verification skipped, a permission widened, a warning suppressed, a sandbox opened
criteria.false: Nothing in `method` does this.

criteria.true: An index, length or offset reaches past the end of a string, array, buffer or typed array. Where the language does not fault on that, the read returns undefined or the write lands somewhere nothing reads, which is harder to notice rather than safer.
criteria.false: Nothing in `method` does this.

criteria.true: Something already closed, aborted, destroyed or released is used again, or released twice. A stream written after it ended, a handle read after close, a controller used after abort, a connection used after it went back to the pool.
criteria.false: Nothing in `method` does this.

criteria.true: A value is read before anything has written it, so what comes back is undefined where a value was meant to be. A field never set, a binding read before its declaration runs, or a result used before the work that produces it has finished.
criteria.false: Nothing in `method` does this.

criteria.true: Arithmetic can wrap, truncate, or change sign, and the result is then used as a size, an index, a length, or a permission
criteria.false: Nothing in `method` does this.

criteria.true: Two paths can reach the same state at once without holding anything, or a check and the act it guards are separated in a way another path can exploit
criteria.false: Nothing in `method` does this.

criteria.true: A value is treated as a type, shape, or variant it may not be: an unchecked cast, a union read through the wrong member, a parsed object trusted to have a shape
criteria.false: Nothing in `method` does this.
